traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 231 Oleaceae, 239 Bignoniaceae, 243 Verbenaceae, 324 Scrophulariaceae, 325 Acanthaceae, 326 Gesneriaceae, 327 Orobanchaceae and 342 Labiatae, the bulk of APG's Lamiales: leaves mostly opposite (alternate in many figworts and broomrapes); stipules absent; flowers mostly zygomorphic, often two-lipped (the olive family's regular); the ovary superior, of two carpels.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Lamiales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): leaves opposite at order level. DELTA (Labiatae, Gesneriaceae) and Wikipedia Gesneriaceae: opposite pairs crossing (decussate) in the big families. 'sometimes spiral' added for the alternate-leaved families (Orobanchaceae, Lentibulariaceae, Plantago, Verbascum), which DELTA gives as spiral. Weighting inferred from the largest families.

traits.stamens.note: Corrects the lamiid value (typical 5) inherited from above. DELTA family pages (read 2026-10-16): Labiatae 2 or 4 (mostly 4, didynamous); Scrophulariaceae s.l. (2-)4(-5); Bignoniaceae usually 4; Gesneriaceae 2 or 4; Oleaceae and Lentibulariaceae 2. APweb core Lamiales node: four didynamous stamens. Typical 4 by species weight.

traits.zygomorphy.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): corolla usually two-lipped in Labiatae, Scrophulariaceae s.l., Gesneriaceae, Lentibulariaceae, often so in Bignoniaceae. Every zygomorphic family with candidates already says bilabiate; this sets the order default.

traits.inflorescence.note: APweb, Lamiales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): inflorescence cymose (determinate). DELTA: Gesneriaceae usually cymose; Wikipedia Gesneriaceae: pair-flowered cymes typical. Racemes and spikes common in Plantaginaceae, Orobanchaceae, Scrophulariaceae.

traits.leaf_division.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): simple in Labiatae (rarely pinnate), Gesneriaceae, Scrophulariaceae s.l. (usually); compound common only in Bignoniaceae (usually) and Oleaceae (simple or pinnate/ternate).

traits.division_pattern.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): compound leaves pinnate in Labiatae and Oleaceae (pinnate or ternate); Bignoniaceae pinnate, palmate, bipinnate or two-foliolate. Palmate kept at 'sometimes' for the Tabebuia group.

traits.rosette.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Labiatae without leaf clusters; basal leaf clusters only in some Scrophulariaceae s.l., Gesneriaceae, Lentibulariaceae and Plantago. Inferred 'usually none' for a largely leafy-stemmed order (Verbascum rosettes are the main exception in Scrophulariaceae).

traits.life_span.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): Oleaceae and Bignoniaceae woody; Gesneriaceae mostly perennial herbs and subshrubs (also Wikipedia Gesneriaceae); Lentibulariaceae perennial; Labiatae and Scrophulariaceae s.l. annual to perennial. 'Usually perennial' inferred from the woody and perennial bulk; annuals concentrated in Linderniaceae (override).

traits.corolla_shape.note: APweb, Lamiales page (read 2026-10-16): calyx connate, stamens fixed to the corolla (a sympetalous tube). DELTA: Labiatae, Scrophulariaceae s.l., Lentibulariaceae corolla a two-lipped tube; Wikipedia Gesneriaceae: petals fused into a tube. Bell and funnel shapes in Bignoniaceae (override); rotate in Veronica/Plantago and Oleaceae (overrides).

traits.hypanthium.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): free hypanthium absent in Labiatae and Gesneriaceae (disk only); no family with candidates states one.

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-16): hermaphrodite in Scrophulariaceae s.l., Orobanchaceae, Bignoniaceae, Lentibulariaceae; mostly so in Labiatae (a few dioecious or polygamous), Gesneriaceae (rarely monoecious) and Oleaceae (usually, else polygamous).
